title: Calcitonin and thyroglobulin
what: This blood test checks two substances made by the thyroid gland. They help the doctor watch thyroid nodules and check how you are after treatment.
why: Calcitonin is checked for thyroid nodules and for relatives if a rare type of thyroid cancer runs in the family. Thyroglobulin is checked after the thyroid has been removed.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 5 days
tell_doctor: If your thyroid was removed or treated with radioactive iodine
If you recently had a thyroid needle biopsy. Thyroglobulin can rise for a while after it
What hormones and medicines you take
If you take vitamins or supplements with biotin. It can affect the result

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Blood is usually taken in the morning on an empty stomach: 8 to 12 hours without food. Plain water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours: no alcohol and no hard workouts. Try not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything needs to change before the test.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A sleeve you can easily roll up above the elbow.

bring: Your referral or list of tests
Past results of these tests. Comparing them matters
Ultrasound reports and your hospital discharge summary after surgery, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow, and you are asked to clench your fist a few times
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick. Blood fills the tubes in a few seconds
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
You can eat after the test
Try to repeat the test at the same lab. That makes results easier to compare
red_flags: The puncture site is very swollen, painful, and red

faq.q: Why are thyroglobulin antibodies tested too?
faq.a: These antibodies can get in the way of measuring thyroglobulin accurately. The doctor needs both results.
Not always. It can be high for other reasons. The doctor will decide if more tests are needed.

reminders.text: Calcitonin and thyroglobulin test tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Water is fine.
